s-cairn.text:
CAIRN — leave a marker; it will still be there

Idea: smooth stones you can almost pick up. The next step sits on the largest stone with its start time resting on top like a marker; the prepared next step is a marker left for your future self; finished tasks stack into a small cairn. Nothing falls over while you are away: pausing never knocks progress down.

Palette: limestone, sage, slate, lichen · Type: Zen Maru Gothic

Weakness / tradeoff: shaded, tactile objects add visual weight and rendering cost, irregular shapes are harder to keep consistent at every size, and the stone metaphor must never turn into a collection game for counting sessions.

s-compare.text:
Compare two concepts

Choose a screen along the top, then a concept above each phone. Both phones are the real boards from the “Five concepts” page, shown at the same 390 × 844 scale.

On the canvas, press Play on this board to use the buttons.

s-daylight.text:
DAYLIGHT — plans live in the light of your actual day

Idea: the day is drawn as the sun’s own circular path, cut by the horizon: daylight above, the evening sinking below. Each next action sits at its cue on that path (16:30 before sunset, the routine after dinner, after sunset), the sun marks now, and the light on every screen comes from it. Glass panels and floating controls in the current iOS idiom. A session dims the room to dusk; finishing brings a sunrise.

Palette: soft sky, glass, sun orange, dusk violet · Type: Geist

Weakness / tradeoff: the most native-feeling direction is also the least ownable; glass over gradients needs care for contrast and performance, and cues without a clock time (“after dinner”) can only be placed approximately on the arc.

s-margin.text:
MARGIN — the next sentence is the interface

Idea: an editorial page instead of app chrome. A serif headline says what to do, typed margin notes carry times and labels, hairline rules replace cards, and exactly one highlighter stroke per screen marks what matters. Navigation is words only; the session is the same page set in ink, with a minute ruler.

Palette: paper, ink, highlighter · Type: Newsreader + IBM Plex Mono

Weakness / tradeoff: very little containment, so controls and states depend on typographic precision; it needs excellent typesetting for Dynamic Type, long names and translation, and some people may find it austere. Word-only tabs are less glanceable than icons.

s-read.text:
How to read this canvas

• Rows are the five concepts, plus Daylight in its dark appearance (row 4b, between Daylight and Cairn). Columns are the same six screens in the same order: 1 Today · 2 Set up a task · 3 Plans · 4 Active session · 5 Session end · 6 Progress. The seventh frame is screen 6 scrolled, with the chart switched to “All time”.
• Every concept uses the same sample content. All numbers are sample data.
• Status bar and home indicator are left to iOS: every layout keeps the top 54 px and the bottom 34 px clear.
• Every session timer shows 18:42 of 25:00 → 25.2 % elapsed, 74.8 % remaining.
• Page “Compare two”: pick any two concepts and one screen, side by side at full size (press Play on that board).

s-thread.text:
THREAD — pick up the thread

Idea: work is one continuous thread. A single soft line links today’s next actions, becomes the hanging thread of the session timer and records progress as a line that rests level in gaps instead of breaking. A yellow bead marks the next thing; tasks are beads, routines are loops.

Palette: cream, indigo, restrained yellow · Type: Figtree

Weakness / tradeoff: the line needs a left gutter, so text columns on Today and Set up are narrower, and the bead/loop meanings must be learned. A long task list would need a collapse rule to keep the thread readable.

s-threshold.text:
THRESHOLD — every start is a small doorway, and it stays open

Idea: the arch is the system’s one shape. Today shows the next action inside a dark doorway with its start time in the crown and Start at the threshold; the session happens inside that room and the doorway outline is the timer. Tasks are doorways (go through once); routines are round windows (come round again).

Palette: plaster, clay, plum night, apricot light · Type: Bricolage Grotesque

Weakness / tradeoff: arches waste space in their crowns and resist long or changing text; the dark hero is bold for a planning screen and could feel heavy, or more like a brand than a tool, after months of daily use.

s-daylight-dark.text:
DAYLIGHT · DARK — the same day, by moonlight

Idea: Daylight’s dark appearance, following the iOS setting. The same circular path, cues and content on a night sky. The moon takes the sun’s place: it marks now on the path and lights the screens, and accents change from sun orange to moonlight silver and violet. The moon is always full, whatever the date: a steady symbol rather than an almanac. Where it sits on the circle is the “now” marker, not its real position in the sky. The session goes one step deeper into the night, and at session end the moon rises behind the sheet.

Palette: night blue, moonlight silver, violet, dark glass · Type: Geist

Weakness / tradeoff: when every screen is dark, the light-planning / dark-focus contrast of the light theme is gone, so the session has to go darker still to feel different. Moonlight is cooler and quieter than the sun, so finishing feels calm rather than celebratory, and the glass layers need extra care to keep text contrast on dark gradients.
